facts.fact: `gpt-6-astra` is the most capable GPT-6 model and the recommended default, with a knowledge cutoff of Apr 30 2026 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models)
`gpt-6.1-sol` is near-Astra at lower cost, with a knowledge cutoff of Apr 30 2026 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models)
`gpt-6.1-terra` is fast and suited to visual reasoning, computer use and writing, with a knowledge cutoff of Jun 1 2026 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models)
`gpt-6-luna` is the most efficient GPT-6 model for high volume, with a knowledge cutoff of May 18 2026 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models)
OpenAI's flagship API models are the GPT-6 family: `gpt-6-astra`, `gpt-6.1-sol`, `gpt-6.1-terra` and `gpt-6-luna` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models)
GPT-6 Astra shipped 2026-09-03 per the API changelog (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)
GPT-6 Sol shipped 2026-09-22 per the API changelog (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)
GPT-6 Luna shipped 2026-09-22 per the API changelog (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)
GPT-6.1 Sol shipped 2026-09-29, with Multi-agent in beta (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)
GPT-6.1 Terra shipped 2026-10-26 per the API changelog (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)
OpenAI cyber models are `gpt-6-cyber` and `gpt-5.6-cyber`, for authorized security work (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models)
OpenAI image models are `gpt-image-2.6-sunburst`, `gpt-image-2.6-flare`, `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` and `gpt-image-2.5-flare` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models)

OpenAI realtime speech models are `gpt-live-1`, `gpt-realtime-2.1`, `gpt-realtime-2.1-mini`, `gpt-realtime-2`, `gpt-realtime-translate` and `gpt-realtime-1.5` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models)
OpenAI transcription models are `gpt-transcribe`, `gpt-live-transcribe` and `gpt-realtime-whisper` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models)
GPT-Rosalind (life sciences) is limited to approved organizations (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models)
`gpt-4.5-preview` shut down 2025-07-14 and `o1-mini` shut down 2025-10-27 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)
`codex-mini-latest` shut down 2026-02-12 and `chatgpt-4o-latest` shut down 2026-02-17 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)
`gpt-4-0314` and `gpt-4-0125-preview` shut down 2026-03-26 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)
The `gpt-4o-realtime-preview`, `gpt-4o-audio-preview` and mini variants shut down 2026-05-07, and `dall-e-2` and `dall-e-3` shut down 2026-05-12 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)

`computer-use-preview`, `gpt-4o-search-preview`, `gpt-5.1-codex-mini`, `gpt-5-codex`, `gpt-5.1-codex`, `gpt-5.1-codex-max`, `gpt-5.2-codex`, `gpt-5-chat-latest`, `gpt-5.1-chat-latest`, `o3-deep-research` and `o4-mini-deep-research` shut down 2026-07-23 (notice 2026-04-22) (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)
`gpt-5.2-chat-latest` and `gpt-5.3-chat-latest` shut down 2026-08-10 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)
The Videos API with `sora-2` and `sora-2-pro` shut down 2026-09-24, with no one-to-one replacement (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)
`gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct`, `babbage-002` and `davinci-002` shut down 2026-09-28, and `gpt-5.4-cyber` shut down 2026-10-01 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)

The `gpt-3.5-turbo`, `gpt-4`, `gpt-4-turbo`, `gpt-4o-2024-05-13`, `gpt-4.1-nano`, `gpt-image-1`, `o1`, `o1-pro`, `o3-mini` and `o4-mini` families shut down 2026-10-23 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)
`/v1/prompts` (reusable prompt objects) shuts down 2026-11-30 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)
The OpenAI Evals platform shuts down 2026-11-30 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)
OpenAI Agent Builder shuts down 2026-11-30 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)
`gpt-image-1-mini`, `gpt-image-1.5` and `chatgpt-image-latest` shut down 2026-12-01 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)
`gpt-5`, `gpt-5-mini`, `gpt-5-nano`, `gpt-5-pro`, `o3` and `o3-pro` shut down 2026-12-11 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)

The replacements for `gpt-5`, `gpt-5-mini`, `gpt-5-nano`, `gpt-5-pro`, `o3` and `o3-pro` (shutting down 2026-12-11) are `gpt-6.1-sol`, `gpt-6.1-terra` and `gpt-6-luna` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)
Self-serve fine-tuning job creation ends 2027-01-06 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)
`tts-1`, `tts-1-hd` and `gpt-4o-mini-tts` shut down 2027-01-06, and `gpt-realtime`, `gpt-audio` and `gpt-realtime-mini` shut down 2027-01-20 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)
`gpt-4o-2024-08-06`, `gpt-4o-2024-11-20`, `gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18`, `gpt-4.1-2025-04-14` and `gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14` shut down 2027-01-14 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)

`gpt-6-luna` is the replacement for `gpt-4o-2024-08-06`, `gpt-4o-2024-11-20`, `gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18`, `gpt-4.1-2025-04-14` and `gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14`, which shut down 2027-01-14 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)

`gpt-image-2` shuts down 2027-02-10; `whisper-1`, the `gpt-4o-*-transcribe` models and `/v1/audio/translations` shut down 2027-02-26; and `gpt-5.1`, `gpt-5.3-codex` and `gpt-5.4-nano` shut down 2027-04-01 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)

As of 2026-11-14 the migration guide states 'While Chat Completions remains supported, Responses is recommended for all new projects' (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/migrate-to-responses)

Responses are stored by default with a 30-day TTL; `store: false` disables storage and is enforced for Zero Data Retention organizations (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/conversation-state)

Chat Completions is still supported as of 2026-11-14: it remains an API status page component and a supported Batch endpoint (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/migrate-to-responses ; https://status.openai.com/)
Chat Completions requests are stored by default for new accounts (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/migrate-to-responses)
The Assistants API was deprecated 2025-08-26 and sunset 2026-08-26, and is 'no longer available' (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)
The replacement for the shut-down Assistants API is the Responses API plus the Conversations API (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/migrate-to-responses)
The Conversations API, together with the Responses API, replaces the Assistants API, sunset 2026-08-26 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/migrate-to-responses)

facts.fact: The Conversations API was released 2025-08-20 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)

A Conversations API conversation object stores items (messages, tool calls, tool outputs), and its ID is passed as the `conversation` parameter on Responses calls; conversation items are not subject to the 30-day response TTL (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/conversation-state)

Alternatives to the Conversations API are chaining with `previous_response_id`, where prior input tokens are still billed, or manual replay (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/conversation-state)
Client-side Responses compaction uses `/responses/compact`, added 2025-12-11 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/conversation-state ; https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)

Server-side Responses compaction uses `context_management` with `compact_threshold` on `/responses` and launched 2026-02-10, together with Skills and the Hosted Shell tool (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)
Compaction is a Responses API feature, client-side via `/responses/compact` or server-side via `context_management` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/conversation-state)

Responses built-in tools are web search (`web_search`), file search (`file_search`), tool search (`tool_search`), remote MCP (`mcp`), function calling (`function`), Shell, Skills, computer use, image generation and Programmatic Tool Calling (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools)
The Responses tools guide gives no per-tool GA/beta status (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools)
The `tool_search` tool requires gpt-5.4 or later (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools)
WebSocket mode for Responses launched 2026-02-23 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)
GPT-5.6 (2026-07-09) brought Programmatic Tool Calling and Multi-agent orchestration (beta) to Responses (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)
Multi-agent orchestration arrived in beta with GPT-5.6 on 2026-07-09 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)
GPT-6 Astra (2026-09-03) brought async tool calling and mid-turn steering controls to Responses (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)
Ultrafast mode for GPT-6.1 Sol arrived 2026-10-08 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)
12-hour prompt caching arrived 2026-10-20 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)

The `code_interpreter` tool's container is `{"type":"auto"}` with `memory_limit` `1g` (default), `4g`, `16g` or `64g`, or an explicit container created through `/v1/containers` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-code-interpreter)
A code interpreter container expires after 20 minutes idle and cannot be reactivated (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-code-interpreter)

The computer use tool is enabled with `tools: [{type: "computer"}]` and emits `computer_call`, `computer_call_output` and `computer_screenshot` items; examples use `gpt-6.1-sol` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-computer-use)
For `gpt-6-astra` OpenAI recommends code execution instead of computer use, though `computer` is still supported (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-computer-use)

Computer use environments are self-run (SDK `ComputerToolset`), partners (Browserbase, Browser Use, Daytona, E2B Desktop) or an OpenAI-hosted browser via the Agents API (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-computer-use)

The file search tool is `{"type":"file_search","vector_store_ids":[...]}` with optional `max_num_results` and metadata `filters`; add `include: ["file_search_call.results"]` to return the raw results (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-file-search)
Files must reach status `completed` (indexed) before they are searchable by file search (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-file-search)
The file search rate limit is 500 RPM on Build and 1000 RPM on Launch/Grow (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-file-search)

Set `background: true` on Responses, then poll while the status is `queued` or `in_progress`, or cancel via the cancel endpoint; use `background` with `stream` to resume streams with `starting_after` (a `sequence_number` cursor) (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/background)
ZDR projects still keep background response data on disk for about 10 minutes (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/background)

The Agents API launched in public beta 2026-09-10 and requires the `OpenAI-Beta: agents=v1` header (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/quickstart ; https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)
The Agents API is at `https://api.openai.com/v1/agents`, for example `POST /v1/agents/sessions` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/quickstart)

OpenAI describes the Agents API as a managed Codex harness with compaction, multi-agent, programmatic tool calling and MCP, with environments `openai_hosted`, `self_hosted` or `none` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents)
Computer use was added to the Agents API 2026-09-29 and scheduled automations 2026-10-23 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)
Agents API data residency is US-only (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/tools)
The Agents API does not support Zero Data Retention, even with a self-hosted sandbox (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/tools)
`multi_agent.max_concurrent_subagents` caps parallel subagents in the Agents API (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/tools)
The OpenAI-hosted Agents API sandbox is billed at container rates (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/tools)
The Python Agents SDK package is `openai-agents` (`pip install openai-agents`; Python >=3.10) (https://pypi.org/pypi/openai-agents/json)
`openai-agents` is at version 0.24.0 on PyPI as of 2026-11-14 (https://pypi.org/pypi/openai-agents/json)

Python Agents SDK primitives are agents, handoffs and agents-as-tools, guardrails (input/output), sessions (memory), tracing, sandbox agents, MCP tools, realtime agents (`gpt-realtime-2.1`) and voice pipelines (https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/)
The Python Agents SDK uses the Responses API by default (https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/)

facts.fact: `@openai/agents` is at 0.22.0 on npm as of 2026-11-14 and depends on `@openai/agents-core`, `@openai/agents-openai` and `@openai/agents-realtime` (https://registry.npmjs.org/@openai/agents/latest)
The TypeScript Agents SDK realtime entry point is `@openai/agents/realtime` (`RealtimeAgent`, `RealtimeSession`, WebRTC/WebSocket transports) (https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/)
The TypeScript Agents SDK MCP classes are `MCPServerStdio`, `MCPServerSSE` and `MCPServerStreamableHttp` (https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/)

`SandboxAgent` (Python and TS) runs in an isolated workspace defined by a `Manifest`, with the capabilities `Shell`, `Filesystem`, `Skills`, `Memory` and `Compaction` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents/sandboxes)

Agents SDK sandbox clients include `UnixLocalSandboxClient`, `DockerSandboxClient`, `E2BSandboxClient`, `ModalSandboxClient` and `DaytonaSandboxClient`, plus Blaxel, Cloudflare, Databricks and Vercel (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents/sandboxes)
`SandboxAgent` is part of the Agents SDK in both Python and TypeScript (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents/sandboxes)

Agent Builder (AgentKit) launched at DevDay 2025-10-06 with ChatKit, its deprecation was announced 2026-06-03, and shutdown is 2026-11-30 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agent-builder ; https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)
To migrate off Agent Builder, export the workflow code (the 'Code' button) to the Agents SDK (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agent-builder)
ChatGPT Workspace Agents is the other migration path for Agent Builder workflows before the 2026-11-30 shutdown (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agent-builder)

ChatKit, an embeddable chat UI, remains available as of 2026-11-14; Agent Builder-hosted workflows (by workflow ID) are supported only through the transition (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/chatkit)
ChatKit packages are `@openai/chatkit-react`, chatkit-js and chatkit-python (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/chatkit)
The recommended path for new ChatKit work is a self-hosted ChatKit server (Python SDK) backed by any agent service, for example the Agents SDK (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/chatkit)
The Evals platform became read-only for existing users 2026-10-31 and shuts down 2026-11-30 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/evals ; https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)

The deprecations page names Promptfoo as the replacement for the Evals platform, and the Evals guide suggests Datasets (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations ; https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/evals)

Fine-tuning is winding down: new users cannot access it, and existing users can create jobs until self-serve job creation ends 2027-01-06 (notice 2026-05-07); fine-tuned models stay usable until their base model is deprecated (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/fine-tuning ; https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)

Supported fine-tuning methods are SFT, DPO (`gpt-4.1-2025-04-14`, `gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14`, `gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14`) and vision (`gpt-4o-2024-08-06`) (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/fine-tuning)

The Realtime API went GA 2025-08-28, and the beta interface (`OpenAI-Beta: realtime=v1`) was removed 2026-05-12 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/realtime ; https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)

Browsers connect to the Realtime API with WebRTC via `/v1/realtime/calls` using an ephemeral secret from `POST /v1/realtime/client_secrets`, while servers use WebSocket (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/realtime)
The Realtime API supports functions, MCP servers and connectors (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/realtime)
Outbound SIP calling for GPT-Live opened to all organizations 2026-11-02 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)
The Decisions API went GA 2026-10-22 with `gpt-6-luna`, after a 2026-10-06 beta; its scope relative to agents was not researched (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)
The Decisions API has been GA since 2026-10-22, after a beta that began 2026-10-06 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)
The Sora/Videos API with `sora-2` and `sora-2-pro` is retired, shut down 2026-09-24 with no one-to-one replacement (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)

Codex runs in the ChatGPT desktop, mobile and web apps, the Codex CLI, the Codex IDE extension and Codex Cloud; builder tools are the Codex SDK, a GitHub Action and non-interactive mode (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs)
Codex integrations cover GitHub, GitLab (beta), Slack and Linear (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs)

Recommended Codex models are `gpt-6-astra`, `gpt-6.1-sol`, `gpt-6.1-terra` and `gpt-6-luna`, with reasoning efforts Light/Low, Medium, High, Extra High, Max and Ultra (subagents) (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/models)
`gpt-6.1-sol` has a 500,000-token default context in Codex (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/models)
`gpt-6.1-terra` in Codex needs Codex CLI 0.159.0 or later and is not available in the IDE extension (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/models)
GPT-5.5 retires from ChatGPT-sign-in Codex 2026-10-14, a retirement that does not affect API-key sessions (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/models)

Comment `@codex review` on a PR, or enable Automatic review in Codex settings, to get a Codex review; `@codex security review` (research preview) runs a security pass (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/third-party/github)
Codex flags only P0/P1 issues in GitHub, and review rules go in a `## Code Review Rules` section of `AGENTS.md` (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/third-party/github)
Codex GitHub code review runs on GitHub pull requests (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/third-party/github)

The OpenAI REST API base URL is `https://api.openai.com/v1`; `OpenAI-Organization` and `OpenAI-Project` headers select the organization and project (https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/overview)
REST API auth is `Authorization: Bearer <API key or workload-identity access token>` (https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/overview)
A workload-identity access token can be used as the bearer credential on the REST API (https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/overview)
Admin endpoints of the REST API need an Admin API key (https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/overview)

The REST version is v1 (`openai-version: 2020-10-01`); every response carries `x-request-id`, and you can send an optional `X-Client-Request-Id` (ASCII, 512 characters or fewer) (https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/overview)

facts.fact: The Python `openai` package is at 3.51.0 on PyPI (Python >=3.10) and reads `OPENAI_API_KEY` (https://pypi.org/pypi/openai/json ; https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/libraries)
The JS/TS SDK is `openai` on npm (Node, Deno, Bun) (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/libraries)

Official OpenAI SDK packages are Python `openai`, JS/TS `openai` (npm), .NET `OpenAI` (NuGet), Java `com.openai:openai-java`, Go `github.com/openai/openai-go/v3` and Ruby gem `openai`, and SDKs read `OPENAI_API_KEY` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/libraries)
There is an `openai` CLI installed via `brew install openai/tools/openai` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/libraries)

The Responses remote MCP tool is declared as `{"type":"mcp","server_label":...,"server_url":...}` with optional `allowed_tools`, `server_description`, `defer_loading` (for tool search), `require_approval` and `authorization`, over Streamable HTTP or HTTP/SSE transports (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp)

The remote MCP tool's `authorization` field takes an OAuth access token, which OpenAI does not store, so it must be resent on every request (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp)

`require_approval` takes `"always"`, `"never"` or `{"never":{"tool_names":[...]}}`, and approval is required by default; the model emits `mcp_approval_request` (`mcpr_...`) and you reply with an `mcp_approval_response` input item (`approve`, `approval_request_id`) using `previous_response_id`, each approval covering one call (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp)
MCP tools are discovered via the `mcp_list_tools` output item, and calls appear as `mcp_call` items (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp)
Responses MCP rate limits are 1000 RPM on Build and 2000 RPM on Launch/Grow (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp)
With the remote MCP tool you pay only tokens for tool definitions and calls, with no per-call fee (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp)

The remote MCP tool is compatible with ZDR and data residency; with `store=true`, data sent to MCP servers is logged for 30 days unless ZDR applies (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp)
The remote MCP tool also works in Chat Completions (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp)

`connector_id` connectors were added to Responses 2025-08-21 and are deprecated for models released after 2026-09-01; older models keep support (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp ; https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)

Connector IDs are `connector_dropbox`, `connector_gmail`, `connector_googlecalendar`, `connector_googledrive`, `connector_microsoftteams`, `connector_outlookcalendar`, `connector_outlookemail` and `connector_sharepoint` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp)
For GitHub, use GitHub's official remote MCP via `server_url` rather than a connector (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp)
Secure MCP Tunnel connects local or private MCP servers to the Responses `mcp` tool via `tunnel_id` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp)
Secure MCP Tunnel was released 2026-05-19 for enterprise customers; a dedicated guide URL was not found (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)

OpenAI's docs MCP server runs at `https://developers.openai.com/mcp` (Streamable HTTP) and gives read-only search and page content over OpenAI developer docs (https://developers.openai.com/learn/docs-mcp)

Add the OpenAI docs MCP server to Codex with `codex mcp add openaiDeveloperDocs --url https://developers.openai.com/mcp`, or `[mcp_servers.openaiDeveloperDocs] url = "https://developers.openai.com/mcp"` in `~/.codex/config.toml` (https://developers.openai.com/learn/docs-mcp)

In the Agents API, MCP servers go in the agent's `tools` array as `type: "mcp"` with `server_label` and a `transport` object (HTTP with `server_url`) (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/tools)
An API key for the Agents API needs the scopes `api.agents.read`, `api.agents.write` and `api.responses.write` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/quickstart)
Using the Agents API needs the `api.agents.write` key scope (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/quickstart)
Using the Agents API needs the `api.responses.write` key scope (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents-api/quickstart)

ChatGPT plugins / Apps SDK are built on MCP: a plugin bundles skills and/or an MCP server, with optional UI, and ChatGPT and Codex share one plugin directory (https://developers.openai.com/plugins/quickstart)

Apps SDK docs moved to the 'ChatGPT plugins and Apps SDK' set at `developers.openai.com/plugins`, and `/apps-sdk` now serves Plugins content (https://developers.openai.com/apps-sdk ; https://developers.openai.com/llms.txt)
Plugin submission goes through the ChatGPT Directory review (https://developers.openai.com/plugins/quickstart)

Apps SDK UI is a `ui://` resource with MIME `text/html;profile=mcp-app`, linked from tools via `_meta.ui.resourceUri`; `_meta["openai/outputTemplate"]` is a ChatGPT compatibility alias (https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/chatgpt-ui)

Apps SDK UI packages are `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps` and `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`, plus optional `@openai/apps-sdk-ui`; `window.openai` extensions (`requestCheckout`, `requestModal`, `uploadFile`, `setWidgetState`) are optional (https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/chatgpt-ui)

To add a custom MCP server in ChatGPT, in ChatGPT Plugins select '+' then 'Add custom MCP server', and set the URL and auth (OAuth, none, or mixed); transports are SSE and streaming HTTP (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/developer-mode ; https://developers.openai.com/plugins/quickstart)

ChatGPT custom MCP servers (developer mode) are labeled 'Elevated risk', and tools without the `readOnlyHint` annotation count as write actions, which require confirmation (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/developer-mode)
OAuth registration for ChatGPT custom MCP servers uses static credentials, CIMD or DCR (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/developer-mode)

facts.fact: Webhooks were added to the OpenAI API 2025-06-24, together with the web search tool; event types were not researched (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/changelog)

Since 2026-06-01, OpenAI models such as `us.openai.gpt-6-sol` and `us.openai.gpt-6-luna` in `us-east-1` and GPT-6 Astra in `us-west-2` are on Bedrock Runtime and Mantle with Responses- and Chat Completions-compatible endpoints (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/amazon-bedrock)
`us.openai.gpt-6-luna` is available on Amazon Bedrock in `us-east-1` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/amazon-bedrock)
GPT-6 Astra is available on Amazon Bedrock in `us-west-2` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/amazon-bedrock)

Remote MCP, hosted file search, the shell tool, image generation, Programmatic Tool Calling and WebSockets are not available for OpenAI models on Amazon Bedrock (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/amazon-bedrock)

OpenAI models including `gpt-6-astra` (2026-09-03), `gpt-6-luna`, `gpt-6-sol` and `gpt-6.1-sol` are sold by Azure as 'Foundry Models sold by Azure', with Azure deployments, regions and auth (pointer only; covered under the Azure/Foundry platform) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/models-sold-directly-by-azure)
No A2A protocol support appeared in the OpenAI API docs reviewed (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/llms.txt)
MCP is the cross-vendor tool protocol across Responses, the Agents SDK, the Agents API, ChatGPT and Codex (unverified) (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/llms.txt)

On Windows install Codex CLI with `npm install -g @openai/codex` (`engines.node >=16`; binary `codex`) or `powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.ps1 | iex"`; macOS/Linux use `curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh | sh` or `brew install --cask codex` (https://github.com/openai/codex ; https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/windows/windows-sandbox)
The Codex Windows page says `winget` 'should be available', not that it is (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/windows/windows-sandbox)

The latest Codex CLI GitHub release is `rust-v0.169.0` (0.169.0 on npm, published Nov 13), licensed Apache-2.0 (https://github.com/openai/codex/releases/latest ; https://registry.npmjs.org/@openai/codex/latest)

Codex CLI 0.169.0 fixed `codex exec` keeping project config and MCP servers disabled in untrusted directories, and Windows sandbox issues with `cmd.exe`/PowerShell (https://github.com/openai/codex/releases/latest)

`codex login` signs in with ChatGPT (browser flow); `printenv OPENAI_API_KEY | codex login --with-api-key` uses an API key (billed at API rates); `codex login --device-auth` (beta) suits headless machines; `codex login status` and `codex logout` check and clear credentials (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth)
`codex login --with-access-token` reads `CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN` and needs admin permission (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth)
Without device auth on a headless machine, copy `~/.codex/auth.json` or forward localhost:1455 to sign in to Codex (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth)

`cli_auth_credentials_store` is `file` (`auth.json` under `CODEX_HOME`, default `~/.codex`), `keyring`, `auto` or `ephemeral`, and admins can force `forced_login_method` (`chatgpt` or `api`) and `forced_chatgpt_workspace_id` (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth)

Under workload identity federation (beta for Codex; `OPENAI_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE`), `codex login` and `codex logout` are rejected (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth ; https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/workload-identity-federation)

Codex user config is `~/.codex/config.toml` and project config is `.codex/config.toml`; profiles are `$CODEX_HOME/<name>.config.toml`, selected with `--profile` (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference)

Project `.codex/config.toml` is loaded only for trusted projects, and project files cannot set `model_provider`, `profiles`, `openai_base_url`, `otel` and similar keys (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference)

`sandbox_mode` is `read-only`, `workspace-write` or `danger-full-access`; `approval_policy` is `on-request`, `never` or `{granular = {...}}`; `approvals_reviewer` is `user` or `auto_review`; and `[sandbox_workspace_write]` takes `writable_roots` and `network_access` (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference ; https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/sandboxing)
The Codex `approval_policy` value `untrusted` is no longer supported and `on-failure` is deprecated (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference)

Codex CLI flags are `--sandbox`/`-s`, `--ask-for-approval`/`-a`, `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`/`--yolo`, `--approve-for-me`/`--not-so-yolo` (on-request plus workspace-write), `-m`, `-p`, `-c key=value`, `-C`, `--search` and `--oss`; subcommands are `exec`, `login`, `logout`, `mcp`, `app-server`, `sandbox`, `resume`, `cloud`, `apply`, `review` and `features` (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/cli/reference)
`--full-auto` is not documented on the Codex CLI reference page (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/cli/reference)

Codex runs natively in PowerShell with `windows.sandbox` set to `mxc` (recommended; needs Windows 11 24H2 build 26100.9278+ or 25H2), `elevated` (sandbox users and firewall rules) or `unelevated`; WSL2 uses the Linux bubblewrap sandbox (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/windows/windows-sandbox ; https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/sandboxing)
IT can pre-provision the Codex Windows sandbox with `codex sandbox setup --elevated --user <identity> --codex-home <path>` (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/windows/windows-sandbox)

facts.fact: Add MCP servers to Codex with `codex mcp add <name> --env K=V -- <command>` (stdio) or `codex mcp add <name> --url <url>` (Streamable HTTP, OAuth via CIMD/DCR); `codex mcp login <name>` signs in and `codex mcp list` lists servers (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp)

`[mcp_servers.<id>]` keys are `command`, `args`, `env`, `url`, `bearer_token_env_var`, `http_headers`, `auth` (`oauth` or `chatgpt`), `enabled_tools`, `disabled_tools`, `default_tools_approval_mode`, `startup_timeout_sec` (default 10) and `tool_timeout_sec` (default 60) (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference)

Codex reads global instructions from `~/.codex/AGENTS.override.md` or `AGENTS.md`, then one file per directory from the Git root down to the cwd (override, then `AGENTS.md`, then `project_doc_fallback_filenames`), concatenated top-down (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/agents-md)
AGENTS.md loading caps at `project_doc_max_bytes` (default 32 KiB) (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/agents-md)
The TypeScript Codex SDK is `@openai/codex-sdk` (Node 18+; `new Codex().startThread().run()`, `resumeThread`) (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/codex-sdk)
The Python Codex SDK is `openai-codex` (Python 3.10+, bundles a pinned CLI; `Codex().thread_start().run()`, `AsyncCodex`) (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/codex-sdk)
`codex mcp-server` has been removed, and the app server (`codex app-server`) is the recommended way to build custom Codex clients (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/codex-sdk)

No official OpenAI Terraform provider or IaC tool appeared in the docs reviewed; projects, keys and users are managed through the Admin API with an Admin API key (unverified as complete) (https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/overview)

facts.fact: Standard rate limits shown 2026-11-14: Build: Astra/Sol/Terra 5,000 RPM and 1M TPM, Luna 5,000 RPM and 2M TPM; Launch: 10,000 RPM and 4M TPM, Luna 10M TPM; Grow: 15,000 RPM and 40M TPM, Luna 30,000 RPM and 180M TPM; limits also apply as RPD, TPD and IPM, and long-context models have separate limits shown in the console (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/rate-limits)

A `429` with `slow_down` can occur within RPM/TPM if traffic ramps too fast; above 1M input TPM, grow traffic by no more than 50% every 15 minutes; failed requests still count against limits (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/rate-limits)

Honor `Retry-After` and the `x-ratelimit-*` headers (including the `-project-tokens` variants); a `503 server_is_overloaded` is not a rate limit, and the SDKs auto-retry eligible 429/503 responses (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/rate-limits)

Batch covers `/v1/responses`, `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/embeddings`, `/v1/completions`, `/v1/moderations`, `/v1/images/generations` and `/v1/images/edits`, with a 24h window and a 50% discount; a batch holds at most 50,000 requests with a 200 MB input file, and you can create 2,000 batches/hour (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/batch)

The per-model Batch queued-token cap is shown only in Platform settings, and outputs expire after 30 days by default (`output_expires_after`, minimum 1 hour) (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/batch ; https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/rate-limits)

Total request headers must stay under 64 KiB and custom header values at or under 60 KiB, and oversized headers may fail with no `x-request-id`; file inputs to models must be under 50 MB per file and 50 MB combined per request (upload with purpose `user_data`) (https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/overview ; https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/file-inputs)
Revoked API keys stop working within seconds, but most other auth changes take up to 15 minutes to propagate (https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/overview)

Top-level `instructions` do not carry over through `previous_response_id`, so resend them every turn; chained input tokens are billed again; in WebSocket mode an uncached ID needs a resend with `previous_response_id: null` and the full input (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/migrate-to-responses ; https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/conversation-state)

The Responses MCP `authorization` token is not stored, so it must be resent on every request, including approval follow-ups; keep `mcp_list_tools` in context to avoid re-listing tools each turn (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp)

Codex MCP default startup timeout is 10 s and tool timeout 60 s; project `.codex/config.toml` (including MCP servers) loads only in trusted projects; ChatGPT web ignores local Codex config and uses plugins; and Codex reads only the first 512 characters of a server's `instructions` reliably (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp)

Codex Windows error `1385` means the sandbox users lack a logon right, which IT must grant; share `CODEX_HOME/.sandbox/sandbox.log` with support but never `.sandbox-secrets/`; if the IDE extension hangs, install VS Build Tools (C++) and the x64 VC++ Redistributable; Windows 10 is best effort (1809+) (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/windows/windows-sandbox)
The Assistants API became Responses plus Conversations (2026-08-26) (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)
Agent Builder moves to the Agents SDK or Workspace Agents (2026-11-30) (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)
Evals moves to Promptfoo (2026-11-30) (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)
`connector_id` connectors move to remote MCP `server_url` for models after 2026-09-01 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-connectors-mcp)

Other OpenAI renames and moves: usage tiers 1–5 became Free/Build/Launch/Grow, the Apps SDK docs set is now 'ChatGPT plugins and Apps SDK', Codex docs moved to learn.chatgpt.com, and `codex mcp-server` was replaced by `codex app-server` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/rate-limits ; https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/codex-sdk)
